factText: Zambia is the historic birthplace of the guided walking safari, pioneered by conservationist Norman Carr in South Luangwa.
caption: World-renowned wildlife sanctuary along the Luangwa River, celebrated as the birthplace of walking safaris.

factText: The name 'Zimbabwe' originates from the Shona phrase 'Dzimba-dza-mabwe', meaning 'large houses of stone', referring to Great Zimbabwe.
caption: Monumental medieval stone city with dry-stone granite walls built without mortar between the 11th and 15th centuries.

factText: The Zimbabwe Bird carved from soapstone at Great Zimbabwe is the national emblem proudly displayed on the flag and coat of arms.
caption: Monumental medieval stone city with dry-stone granite walls built without mortar between the 11th and 15th centuries.

factText: Mana Pools National Park along the lower Zambezi River is famed for elephants that stand on their hind legs to reach high acacia pods.
caption: Zimbabwe's largest natural reserve, home to one of Africa's largest elephant populations and wild dog packs.

factText: Australia is the only continent covered entirely by a single nation and is home to unique marsupials like kangaroos, koalas, and wombats.
caption: Kangaroos and native marsupials across the Australian continent.

factText: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest living structure on Earth, composed of over 2,900 individual reefs and 900 islands.
caption: The Great Barrier Reef, the largest living coral structure on Earth.

factText: The 180-degree meridian (International Date Line) passes right through Taveuni, Fiji, allowing visitors to stand with one foot in 'today' and one in 'yesterday'.
imageTitle: Bouma National Heritage Park in Taveuni
caption: Protected rainforest on the 'Garden Island' of Taveuni featuring the three cascading Tavoro Waterfalls.

factText: Millennium Island (Caroline Atoll) in Kiribati is the first place on Earth to welcome the rising sun each new calendar year.
caption: One of the largest marine protected reserves on Earth, conserving pristine deep ocean ecosystems and corals.

factText: Kiribati consists of 33 coral atolls and reef islands dispersed across an ocean expanse larger than India.
caption: One of the largest marine protected reserves on Earth, conserving pristine deep ocean ecosystems and corals.

factText: The Marshallese people were master navigators who created traditional 'stick charts' (rebbelib and mattang) to read ocean wave swells.
caption: Slender ribbon of coral islands enclosing a calm 295-sq-km emerald lagoon plied by traditional outrigger canoes.

factText: The bikini swimwear was named in 1946 after Bikini Atoll in the Marshall Islands, capturing global attention like an atomic blast.
caption: Slender ribbon of coral islands enclosing a calm 295-sq-km emerald lagoon plied by traditional outrigger canoes.

factText: The Marshall Islands established the world's largest shark sanctuary in 2011, covering nearly 2 million square kilometers of ocean.
caption: Tranquil outer atoll celebrated for traditional coconut copra production, shark sanctuaries, and marine life.

factText: Nan Madol on Pohnpei is the only ancient city ever constructed entirely on top of a coral reef, using basalt stone columns weighing tons.
caption: The 'Venice of the Pacific', an ancient stone city built atop 92 artificial islets linked by tidal canals off Pohnpei.

factText: Yap Island is famous for Rai stones, the world's largest stone money discs, quarried in Palau and paddled across hundreds of miles of ocean.
caption: Historic limestone circular carved stones measuring up to 3.6 meters across, still used for ceremonial transactions.

factText: The Federated States of Micronesia comprises 607 islands spread across nearly 2.7 million square kilometers of the western Pacific.
caption: Historic limestone circular carved stones measuring up to 3.6 meters across, still used for ceremonial transactions.

factText: Nauru is the smallest independent sovereign republic in the world, covering a mere 21 square kilometers (8.1 sq miles).
caption: Pristine white sand beach framed by dramatic limestone pinnacle reefs on the eastern Pacific shore of Nauru.

factText: New Zealand has more sheep than people—approximately five sheep for every human resident.
imageTitle: Sheep Grazing on New Zealand Pastures
caption: New Zealand has approximately five sheep for every human resident across its green hills.

factText: Visitors to Palau must sign the 'Palau Pledge' stamped into their passports, swearing to tread lightly and preserve the island environment.
caption: The Palau fruit dove is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.

factText: In 2009, Palau created the world's very first dedicated National Shark Sanctuary, banning all commercial shark fishing in its EEZ.
caption: The Palau fruit dove is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.

factText: Palau is renowned for Jellyfish Lake, where swimmers can safely snorkel with millions of stingless golden jellyfish.
caption: Isolated marine lake populated by millions of golden jellyfish that lost their stinging ability over evolutionary time.

factText: Papua New Guinea is the most linguistically diverse country on Earth, with over 840 living indigenous languages spoken.
caption: The highest mountain in Papua New Guinea (4,509 m), featuring glacial alpine valleys and equatorial tarns.

factText: It is home to the stunning Birds of Paradise, whose elaborate plumage and courtship dances are celebrated in tribal Sing-Sing festivals.
caption: The Raggiana bird-of-paradise, also known as Count Raggi's bird-of-paradise, is a large bird in the bird-of-paradise family Paradisaeidae.

factText: Marovo Lagoon in the Solomon Islands is the largest saltwater lagoon protected by a double barrier reef on Earth.
caption: The world's largest saltwater double-barrier lagoon, dotted with hundreds of forested coral islets in New Georgia.

factText: Every winter, hundreds of southern humpback whales migrate from Antarctica to the warm sheltered waters of Tonga to calve.
caption: Sheltered tropical island channels where migratory Antarctic humpback whales mate and nurse newborn calves.

factText: Vanuatu has the world's only underwater post office, located 3 meters beneath the surface in Hideaway Island's marine sanctuary.
caption: The Vanuatu flying fox or white flying fox is a species of flying fox in the family Pteropodidae.

factText: Antarctica is the coldest, windiest, and driest continent on Earth, containing approximately 90% of all the ice and 70% of all freshwater on the planet.
caption: The southernmost active volcano on planet Earth, renowned for its persistent boiling anorthoclase phonolite lava lake.

factText: Emperor penguins are the only animal species that remain on the open Antarctic sea ice throughout the brutal, sunless polar winter to breed.
imageTitle: Emperor Penguins on Antarctic Sea Ice
caption: Emperor penguins endure the sub-zero Antarctic winter ice pack to breed and rear their chicks.

factText: Nikola Tesla, the pioneering electrical engineer who invented alternating current (AC) power, was of Serbian heritage.
caption: Nikola Tesla, pioneering electrical engineer who invented alternating current (AC) power.
